_comment: Thresholds for the staging lint — the check that answers 'this will render, but it will look wrong'. Every number here was derived by measuring the shipped corpus, not invented. FALSE POSITIVES ARE THE ENEMY: a lint that fires on a film you already approved gets switched off within a week, so a rule earns its place only if it stays silent on all five shipped stories except where they are genuinely broken.

faceOccluded._comment: Something in front of a character covers their face. Body coverage cannot be the test: the car dashboard covers ~31% of the cast's BODIES and 0% of their faces, which is correct, while ts_prop_door covered ~31% of Nan's FACE, which was a bug. Same number, opposite verdict — so the face is what gets measured.
faceOccluded._authored_comment: An authored reveal is not a bug — the wall closing over Fortunato in The Last Cask IS that film's climax. Provenance is scoped to the SCENE, not the shot, because pose tracks are rebuilt per shot (ToonProject.swift:967) and a wall that was cued in shot 2 is still standing in shot 4 with no cue of its own. If the occluder is cued anywhere in the scene and started the scene clear, the coverage is deliberate.

feetCropped._comment: A locomotion clip puts the performance in the legs. Framing that cuts them off leaves a torso sliding along with nothing driving it — the floating-torso read. Only fires while a clip is actually running, so a seated or waist-up dialogue shot is never flagged.

gestureShadowed._comment: The trap that cost the most time to find. Every line beat sets pose 'talk', and the named pose layers OVER the motion clip, so 'talk' — which claims armL/armR/head on every shipped rig — silently erases a wave or a point running underneath it. The cue is accepted, nothing errors, and the gesture just does not happen. Hand-authored poseParts is the one layer that outranks it.

cuePastShotEnd._comment: A cue whose start is beyond its shot's measured duration. Silently clamped at compile, so it fires at the wrong moment instead of failing. Common after re-voicing, when every line's real length differs from the estimate the cue was written against.

effectOnAbsentTarget._comment: An effect spawned on a character who is not staged, hidden, or already gone. Draws at stage centre instead of on them.

travelNoOp._comment: A scene declares motion but no backdrop layer can express it — every layer either has travels:false or no loop/recede period. The camera says the world is moving and the world does not move.

speakerOffFrame._comment: A character MID-LINE who cannot be seen. Deliberately narrower than "anyone off frame": a single or an over-shoulder leaves the other party outside the frame by design, and 15 of the first 19 firings of the broader rule were exactly that.
